requirements: Define a canonical package/seam/lane/promotion object family and extend schemas beyond node-level modeling.
Unify requested/effective execution identity to include account identity, fallback/switch reasons, and overseer-role semantics.
Define package-based lane-pool/worktree policy end-to-end, including contamination, restore, safe-point, and shared visibility.
Preserve historical lane/worktree lineage after cleanup/remove/archive and keep lineage queryable in graph/history/audit views.
Limit Orchestrator widget composition to Progress tab; keep Seams/Node Graph/Evidence/History/Ledger as native fixed-purpose surfaces.
decisions: Source Control remains worktree-first; Orchestrator remains package/seam/lane-first.
Orchestrator initiates scoped lane/worktree actions while Source Control executes Git-native mutations.
Lane is primary operational object; worktree is backing filesystem/Git asset and may be removed while lane history persists.
Adopt one canonical HITL model and one canonical recovery action family across UI/runtime/chat.
Replace GitHub login as stable key with internal account_id; treat login/provider_account_id as provider-native disclosure metadata.
data_shapes: Missing canonical IDs/keys across contracts: project_id, attempt_id, package_id, seam_id, lane_id, worktree_id, safe_point_id, promotion_class.
HITL payload drift: allowed_actions[] vs allowed_action_ids[].
Lifecycle vocabulary needed for lane/worktree: baseline, active, suspect, restoring, retained, cleanup_eligible, archived, removed, historical.
Widget projection contracts should be projection/record-based (run summary, blockers, seam/package/lane health) rather than tier events.
routing_rules: Use three-tier cleanup routing: Priority 1 canonical contract blockers, Priority 2 misleading UI/SCM docs, Priority 3 terminology/anti-drift docs.
Route blocked/major decisions Dashboard -> Orchestrator -> chat-thread with consistent runtime action families.
Route Git/worktree mutation operations through Source Control even if launched contextually from Orchestrator.
Constrain widget hostability to Dashboard/Usage/Orchestrator-Progress and prevent deep-inspection tabs from becoming generic widget canvases.
verification_rules: Scheduler contracts must converge to one model (eliminate lexicographic vs scored vs UI-derived coexistence).
Identity contract consumers must render canonical requested/effective fields and stop consuming deprecated _id persona canonical forms.
Projection freshness/trust-state must be persisted as a shared contract and used for action gating/fallback behavior.
Cleanup/archive/remove flows must preserve historical references and remediation linkage rather than deleting visibility.
owner_consumer_obligations: Contracts_V0 should remain identity SSOT; downstream UI/storage/provider docs must align field names and semantics.
Orchestrator owns lane/package governance truth; Source Control owns worktree/Git execution and operator actions.
Provider/Persona/Prompt docs must retire tier-era ownership language and model package/seam/lane-aware execution identity.
Permissions model must include execution-entity/lane/package/account scoping for approvals and carryover behavior.
stale_retirement_items: Retire tier-first/tier-widget assumptions in Orchestrator_Page, Widget_System, Run_Graph_View, and related UI docs.
Retire schema/document assumptions that only model run/node/tier without seam/package/lane/promotion/account lineage.
Deprecate stale widget layout keys for non-Progress Orchestrator tabs and replace with native tab view-state persistence.
open_questions: Will tier terms become compatibility UI aliases only, or be fully deprecated from runtime/orchestration contracts?
How should package overseer vs seam overseer authority be partitioned across scheduling/review/promotion/recovery?
For bridged runtimes, is upstream account switching capturable, intentionally opaque, or a hard capability gap?
What is the final canonical blocked/recovery action taxonomy used by UI/runtime/chat equally?
What exact projection trust/freshness record family should govern degraded-mode behavior?
process_defects: Contradictory scheduler models (lexicographic vs scored ready-set vs UI-derived recovery).
Contradictory HITL boundaries (tier-boundary vs blocked-node/runtime-overlay vs mid-tier approval nodes).
Conflicting identity field semantics across contracts/UI/provider docs, including persona _id and provider_account_id drift.
Parallel SCM/worktree ownership models conflict (run/tier/subtask vs package-lane pools).
Planning machinery drift exists in support artifacts (e.g., chunk-line fallback disagreement).
doc_hints: High-impact rewrites concentrate in Orchestrator_Page, Executor_Protocol, Contracts_V0, storage-plan, human-in-the-loop, graph schemas, WorktreeGitImprovement.
Source Control panel is constrained; prefer compact row metadata plus deep links rather than full governance context in-panel.
Keep History and Ledger semantically separate (chronology vs exact-record inspection).
